xsendfile.title: X-Sendfile
xsendfile.subtitle: Let the web server send videos and large files for your PHP app.
xsendfile.builtIn: Built in: nothing to install or turn on

what.title: What it is for
what.body: Normally PHP reads a protected file and sends it itself, byte by byte. A long video keeps a PHP worker busy for the whole playback. With X-Sendfile, PHP only checks who may see the file and answers with one header that names it. dPanel's web server then sends the file.
what.p1: Videos start and seek faster: byte ranges are answered at once.
what.p2: PHP workers are freed in milliseconds, so the site stays fast under load.
what.p3: Private files stay private: keep them outside public/ and give them no URL.
what.p4: Downloads can be resumed, and use almost no PHP memory.

how.title: How it works
how.s1: The browser asks your app for a file, for example /media/12/video.
how.s2: Your PHP code checks the login or payment, then sends an X-Sendfile header with the file's full path.
how.s3: dPanel sends the file, with byte ranges, and keeps your other headers (type, download name, caching).

rules.title: Rules
rules.r1: The path must be absolute, for example /home/{user}/media/video.mp4.
rules.r2: The file must be inside the website owner's home folder (/home/{user}) and owned by that user. Symlinks are followed to where they really point.
rules.r3: Any other file gets 404 Not Found, so a site can never send another site's or the server's files.
rules.r4: Send no body with the header; dPanel replaces it with the file.
rules.r5: Content-Type, Content-Disposition, Cache-Control and cookies from PHP are kept.

examples.title: How to use it
examples.laravelNote: If your app has a setting for it, such as MEDIA_XSENDFILE=true or XSENDFILE=true in .env, turning it on is enough.
examples.wordpressNote: WooCommerce: WooCommerce → Settings → Products → Downloads → File download method → X-Accel-Redirect/X-Sendfile. Easy Digital Downloads and other download plugins have a similar option.

check.title: Check that it works
check.body: Ask for a small part of a file through your app. A 206 Partial Content answer with a Content-Range header means dPanel sent it.
check.look: Expected: HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content and content-range: bytes 0-99/…

apache.title: My app asks for Apache mod_xsendfile
apache.body: dPanel serves websites with its own web server, not Apache, so there is no module to install. Apps written for mod_xsendfile work as they are: turn on their X-Sendfile setting and keep the files inside the site owner's home folder.
